newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields close lower on CPI-hopes.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields close lower on CPI-hopes.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell several basis points on Monday following a strong German market and on optimistic hopes for Sweden's consumer price index (CPI) for December due out on Tuesday.
Short maturities were almost unchanged. "People have bought ahead of the CPI-figure and we have narrowed the spread against Germany," one dealer said.
"The strengthening of the crown against the mark also helped."
The crown strengthened a little initially but was later driven down by the weakening Finnish markka.
The crown weakened to 4.3620 crowns to the mark compared to 4.3570 late on Friday.
Dealers said the key focuses for Tuesday were the CPI due at 0815 GMT which was expected to be -0.3 percent for the month as well as for the year and the Riksbank's repo tender at 0830 GMT.
The market was expecting a cut of 15 to 25 basis points from the current repo rate of 4.10 percent, a Reuter survey found.
"There is going to be a lot of disappointment if the Riksbank does not cut the repo rate," one dealer said.
November's current account presented on Monday showed a 6.3 billion crowns surplus.-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
